address.streetAddress: 17 Science Museum Road, Tsim Sha Tsui East

ld.name: Hotel ICON Hong Kong in Hong Kong
ld.description: Here the high-volume name is justified: Hotel ICON is an ambitious project, with orthography to match. For starters, the team behind the hotel is comprised of international design stars. Space prohibits us from listing them all, but suffice to say that Sir Terence Conran is at the top of the marquee, while relatively minor details such as the flora are handled by the likes of the eminent French botanist Patrick Blanc. (For the record, it’s not just any old flower arrangement, but a visually striking vertical garden — a bloom of green against all the gleaming white marble of a soaring lobby.)

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Upper House Hong Kong in Hong Kong Island
ld.description: Hong Kong’s upscale hotels scale dizzying heights of luxury, and lately its more adventurous boutiques have been setting the bar high for style. And now there are hotels that do a bit of both: Upper House Hong Kong, with over a hundred rooms, is bigger than a boutique hotel, and its crisp-edged Chinese modernist look, courtesy of designer André Fu, is quite a lot more sober than some of the whimsical little designers’ hotels.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Victoria Dockside, 18 Salisbury Rd, Tsim Sha Tsui

ld.name: Rosewood Hong Kong in Kowloon
ld.description: A new luxury hotel opening in Hong Kong is a major event, given the quality of the competition. And this is more than just an everyday opening — Hong Kong is the Rosewood group’s home, which means this brand-new 65-story skyscraper on the Kowloon waterfront is the brand’s new global flagship. If you want a picture of the state of the luxury hotelier’s art circa 2020, then look no further.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

pages.h1: The Murray, Hong Kong, a Niccolo Hotel

ld.name: The Murray, Hong Kong, a Niccolo Hotel in Hong Kong Island
ld.description: It’s rare that a brand new hotel rockets straight to the top of Hong Kong’s hospitality scene, and rarer still, for obvious reasons, that it’s converted from a late-Sixties landmark government building by the eminent London-based architects Foster + Partners. But, as is by now clear, the Murray is no ordinary hotel. The original structure is oddly well-suited to luxury-hotel use — its recessed, angled windows keep direct sunlight to a minimum, which helps to cool the rooms. And Foster + Partners made significant improvements as well, and not just in interior design — they opened up the ground level to street life, for one thing, a concern that the original government ministry didn’t share.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: International Commerce Centre, 1 Austin Road West

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong in Kowloon
ld.description: Occupying the top 16 floors of the International Commerce Centre, this hotel remains one of the highest in the world. The spacious, elegant bedrooms have subtle Asian influences in their decoration and most of the suites have harbour and mountain views. The indoor swimming pool is on the 118th floor, as is the cool Ozone bar, making it the highest rooftop bar in the world.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Hong Kong in Hong Kong Island
ld.description: Come to think of it, it is a little bit hard to believe there hasn’t been a Four Seasons here for almost a decade. But it’s a good thing there wasn’t, because now we get to watch as the venerable luxury chain makes its grand re-entrance into the Hong Kong market. And this truly is an impressive one — new hotels are rare here, and still rarer is the kind of expansive space this Four Seasons offers.
ld.petsAllowed: \n The hotel does not welcome pets.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Mandarin Oriental The Landmark, Hong Kong

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental The Landmark, Hong Kong in Hong Kong Island
ld.description: The original Mandarin Oriental on Hong Kong island just about cornered the market on over-the-top classic luxury. No surprise, then, that Mandarin Oriental The Landmark, over in Central, is a little bit different. It’s a contemporary masterpiece in a town where tastes run conservative — the redesigned façade by Neri&Hu and the interiors by Joyce Wang Studio are very near the cutting edge of modern luxury.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Peninsula Hong Kong in Kowloon
ld.description: The Peninsula is the original Hong Kong luxury hotel, still its grandest, and is the archetypal Asian colonial hotel, still serving afternoon tea, British Empire style, in its massive gilded lobby. You have not experienced truly world-class service until you have been waited on by an army of attentive hotel staffers — in places like these you half expect to be fanned with a giant palm frond, or carried from place to place by a team of bellhops; but don't fret, for as soon as you need privacy, they will vanish without a trace.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Hong Kong in Hong Kong Island
ld.description: The original Mandarin Oriental is back. Though it’s always been one of the best hotels in Hong Kong, if not all of Asia, this relic of the Swinging Sixties was beginning to show its age. Now, after a thorough rethink of its interiors (and not just a cosmetic one — we’re talking walls knocked down, floors ripped up, the works) it’s got the looks to once again match its reputation.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Park Hyatt Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: We’ve heard that Shenzhen is the capital of the future, and based on the quality of the city’s Park Hyatt, we’re inclined to believe it. It’s a tower-topping luxury hotel designed by Yabu Pushelberg, whose rooms and suites are as lavish as any in the game, and have extraordinary views of central Shenzhen through floor-to-ceiling windows. As in any Park Hyatt you can assume you’ll find a well-equipped spa, a well-lit indoor pool, and a generous handful of restaurants and bars, including the Attic, a speakeasy-style bar at the apex of this pointed 48-story tower.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: UpperHills Block A, No. 5001 Huanggang Road, Futian District, Guangdong

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: Knowing the parties involved, you might expect a Mandarin Oriental hotel in Shenzhen, China to be almost preposterously luxurious, and if that’s your instinct, you won’t be led astray. It occupies, as these things so often do, the highest floors of a 79-story skyscraper, this one right in the heart of the Futian business district. The style is stately as ever — handsome and contemporary, but equally palatable to design fans and business-hotel traditionalists. The rooms are ultra-luxe, though tastefully so, as is the 68th-floor spa; the hotel’s eight restaurants and bars include the much-in-demand Bay by Chef Fei.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Andaz Shenzhen Bay in Shenzhen
ld.description: Andaz Shenzhen Bay finds itself in a particularly lively corner of China’s coastal megalopolis, surrounded by brand-new office towers and high-tech headquarters galore. Designer Tony Chi brings a bit of New York style to this outpost of Hyatt’s upscale luxury-boutique brand; the rooms are clean-lined and contemporary, but warmed by old-world touches like leather chairs and marble baths. The views of the city and the bay are impressive, as are the hotel’s facilities — from its 19-meter indoor pool to its twin restaurants, East Room and West Room, named not only for their spatial orientation but for their culinary inspirations as well.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The St. Regis Hong Kong in Hong Kong Island
ld.description: The St. Regis hotels often err too much on the side of tastefulness, but the St. Regis Hong Kong, thanks to the attention of the celebrated local designer André Fu, adds just the right measure of flamboyance to breathe new life into the recipe. Along with its design-hotel good looks it’s got all the luxury-hotel comforts: spacious bedrooms with dramatic views, swanky bathrooms with soaking tubs, and an extensive Athletic Club and Spa. Restaurants include chef Olivier Elzer’s Michelin-starred L’Envol, the Drawing Room for afternoon tea, and the elegant New York–inspired St. Regis Bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: T7, No.1 Shenzhen Bay, No. 3008, Zhongxin Road, Nanshan District

ld.name: Raffles Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: Raffles has come a long way since its 19th-century beginning in colonial Singapore; here the brand occupies the prominent central tower of the ultra-modern mixed-use One Shenzhen Bay complex. Raffles Shenzhen, however, is neither entirely historical nor entirely futuristic, but blends elements of both worlds; rooms and suites contain classic elements, for example, even as they look out over Shenzhen Bay from an astonishing height.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The St. Regis Shenzhen Bao'an in Shenzhen
ld.description: Shenzhen's Bao'an District occupies the western edge of the Pearl River Delta, looking out over Qianhai Bay toward Hong Kong. The St. Regis arrived here in February 2025, bringing its second address in the city: 289 rooms across 51 floors where dark oak parquet, Carrara marble bathrooms and intricate marquetry woodwork give the interiors a weight and craftsmanship that the building's glass exterior doesn't hint at. Emerald-hued sofas and sweeping bay views define the living areas. Yan Ting does seasonal Cantonese; the Drawing Room on the 35th floor, framed around Caroline Astor lore, serves afternoon tea, and the rooftop terrace bar is where the city comes into focus.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: No. 5016 Shennan Road East, Luohu District

ld.name: The St. Regis Shenzhen in Shenzhen
ld.description: Where better than 100 stories above China’s unofficial high-tech capital for the St. Regis brand to find a harmonious blend of its storied past and its optimistic future? The St. Regis Shenzhen stands atop the Kingkey 100 skyscraper, from which its 290 rooms and suites take in extraordinarily far-ranging views. The interiors admit of a wealth of stylistic influences, from Art Deco to street art, and the resulting atmosphere is both glamorous and memorable. Butler service is among the benefits, and the six restaurants and bars are supplemented by the city’s many ground-level offerings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: The St. Regis Macao The Londoner Macao, Estrada do Istmo, s/n,, Cotai, Macau SAR, P.R. China

ld.name: The St. Regis Macao in Macau
ld.description: Everything about the St. Regis Macao is carefully designed to evoke the elegance of an earlier time, right down to the classical spelling of the city’s name. While the décor is contemporary, it’s richly historical as well, incorporating nods to Macau’s history as a Portuguese seaport. The rooms range from expansive to downright sprawling, and the comforts are extravagant as well.
ld.petsAllowed: The hotel maintains a strict no-pets policy.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Galaxy Macau, Estrada da Baía da Nossa Senhora da Esperança, s/n, COTAI

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Macau in Macau
ld.description: All bedrooms are suites at the exclusive Ritz-Carlton hotel, which is located on the upper floors at Galaxy Macau. They are impeccably dressed and come with particularly luxurious marble bathrooms. They also provide great views of Cotai, as does the outdoor pool. Along with a state-of-the-art spa is an elegant bar and stylish, very comfortable lounges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Galaxy Macau Resort, Avenida Marginal Flor de Lotus, Cotai

ld.name: Banyan Tree Macau  in Macau
ld.description: If you’re familiar with Banyan Tree’s success at bringing the private-villa concept to some of Asia’s most desirable coastal real estate, their foray into Macau may at first seem a bit odd. After all, the densely populated region’s status as something like the Vegas of the East — with all the attendant glitz that nickname suggests — doesn’t exactly scream “eco-resort.” But Banyan Tree has proven quite adept at making its style work in disparate places, and here the hotel slots itself comfortably into the Galaxy Macau casino, carving out a generous 246 suites that take the experience into the sky.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Estrada da Baia de N. Senhora, Esperanca, SN

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Macao in Cotai
ld.description: If the Four Seasons Hotel Macao, Cotai Strip looks a bit like something straight out of Monte Carlo, the resemblance is not entirely accidental — the Cotai Strip is Macau’s answer to Monte Carlo, or perhaps Las Vegas. From the exterior this Four Seasons is perhaps more Vegas than French Riviera, but once inside the lobby, under the rotunda, you’ll certainly be struck by the heavily European Casino Royale atmosphere of it all.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Rua do Tiro 澳門上葡京

ld.name: Grand Lisboa Palace Macau in Cotai
ld.description: Neither “grand” nor “palace” is an overstatement — the Grand Lisboa Palace Macau is a truly vast luxury resort in Cotai, Macau’s answer to the Vegas Strip. With 1,350 rooms it’s dizzying in its scale, and it finds space within its walls for the Bazar, a luxury mall with more than 100 retailers. The rooms and suites are ornate and colorful, blending historical Chinese and Portuguese elements with crisp contemporary design and modern luxuries. There’s a spa on a suitably large scale as well as a vast European-style garden, and a list of restaurants and bars would exhaust this description’s modest wordcount.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Londoner Hotel, Macau in Cotai
ld.description: With just shy of six thousand rooms, the Londoner Resort is something like a hundred times the size of the typical boutique hotel. Within this vast resort, the 600-suite Londoner Hotel feels practically intimate. Here you’ll find an atmosphere that’s perhaps more thoroughly London than the English capital itself; it’s got suites named for members of the royal family as well as 14 suites designed by David Beckham as a tribute to his own personal lifestyle. A vast casino and retail complex are close at hand, and inside the Londoner itself are a pair of famous Chinese restaurants as well as the very British Churchill’s Table.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Rua do Tiro 澳門路氹射擊路

ld.name: The Karl Lagerfeld in Cotai
ld.description: The legendary fashion designer Karl Lagerfeld never made it to Macau to see his namesake hotel in person, but he designed its interiors from top to bottom, and his presence is everywhere. It’s an unapologetically glamorous experience, and its rooms are marked by what might be a surprising deference to classic Chinese interior design — filtered, of course, through the Lagerfeld sensibility. The spa and health club are suitably lavish, and the restaurant, Mesa by José Avillez, makes the most of Macau’s Portuguese connection. Meanwhile the Book Lounge is inspired by Mr. Lagerfeld’s own home library and features four thousand books hand-selected by the designer himself.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: City of Dreams - Morpheus in Cotai
ld.description: This hotel, part of the City of Dreams, is set to become a landmark in Cotai. It's architecturally stunning exterior was designed by the late Dame Zaha Hadid. Its interior is no less striking with a rooftop pool, a spa and numerous eateries, including two restaurants from Alain Ducasse. Bedrooms are luxurious, beautifully styled and equipped with the latest technology.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Palazzo Versace Macau in Cotai
ld.description: Rarely has a hotel’s name brought with it such promise of elegance and style. Thankfully, Palazzo Versace lives up to its title, dripping with gloriously maximalist chic. Ornate doesn’t even begin to cover it, with a mosaic-emblazoned pool, chandeliers, and enough plush furnishings to last you a lifetime. It sits within the Grand Lisboa Palace, a jaw-droppingly grand construction and Macau’s tallest building. For dinner, transport yourself to the Amalfi Coast at Don Alfonso 1890.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: No. 25, Lane 27, Section 4, Ren'ai Road, Da'an District

ld.name: Kimpton Da An Taipei in Da’an District
ld.description: Kimpton’s growth from a California phenomenon into a nationwide and now global boutique-hotel brand hasn’t diluted its appeal — thanks to designers Neri & Hu, the Kimpton Da An Hotel in Taipei might just be the most stylish of the bunch. It’s an adaptation of an apartment complex in this hip city-center neighborhood, and the residential feeling remains, though it’s made livelier by its restaurant, Tavernist, overseen by a Noma alum, as well as Kimpton’s trademark daily social hour, where your hosts provide wine, light bites, and conversation. Spare a moment for the rooftop terrace, with its expansive views of the city.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: InterContinental Kaohsiung in Kaohsiung City
ld.description: The southern Taiwanese port city of Kaohsiung may not quite be on Taipei’s level as an international destination, but a hotel like the InterContinental Kaohsiung means visitors can expect world-class luxury hospitality. It’s part of the Asia New Bay Area waterfront redevelopment, and is surrounded not only by corporate headquarters but by significant cultural destinations as well, including the Kaohsiung Exhibition Center and a Music Center containing several concert halls; your neighbors at the InterContinental might be visiting executives, but they might just as easily be concert pianists or K-pop singers.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: No. 139 Dunhua North Road, Songshan District

ld.name: Capella Taipei in Songshan District
ld.description: Capella Taipei styles itself a “modern mansion,” and it’s not hard to see their point — the line between top-tier luxury hotel and luxe private residence is not always sharply focused. It helps that the designer is André Fu, the man responsible for a good share of the world’s swankiest hotels. Here the interiors are dazzling yet understated, and feel like spaces you could easily spend more than a few nights in.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: No. 16, Wenquan Lane, Section 1, Dongguan Road, 424, Heping District

ld.name: Hoshinoya Guguan in Taichung City
ld.description: Japan’s Hoshinoya hotel group knows a thing or two about onsen baths; for their first overseas expansion they’ve chosen a valley in the Central Mountains of Taiwan, a place with hot springs of its own. Like a Japanese ryokan, Hoshinoya Guguan has both public baths and in-room private ones; it’s also got jaw-dropping views of the verdant scenery, and stunning interiors in its tranquil, luxurious rooms and suites. Meals, too, are presented in kaiseki style, with multiple courses all meticulously composed — proof not only that the ryokan experience can be modernized, but that it travels well, too.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Taipei in Taipei
ld.description: Forget modern, forget skyscrapers, forget the trend of Asian luxury hotels in gleaming glass towers. The Mandarin Oriental, Taipei may be a new build, but in spirit it’s straight out of the Thirties. In this it may be even more impressive than the typical Mandarin Oriental — which, it scarcely needs pointing out, is not an unimpressive thing to begin with. They don’t just vaguely gesture in the direction of Art Deco, in the way a more pedestrian luxury hotel might — here they practically bow down before it. Instead of a sort of modern-translation equivalent of a classic luxury hotel, this is absolutely the genuine article.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Lalu in Sun Moon Lake
ld.description: Located in the geographic center of Taiwan, Sun Moon Lake is a spectacular, partially man-made wonder. Before 1934, it was two shallow, marshy lakes, one in the shape of the sun, the other resembling a crescent moon, with an island in between — the island of Lalu, home to the indigenous Shao people. But the construction of a hydroelectric plant during the Japanese occupation filled the basin, deepening the lake from 20 feet to 60, and drastically shrinking the island of Lalu. The Shao people were moved to a village at the edge of the newly merged Sun Moon Lake, and the island remains to this day a site for Shao ancestor worship, off-limits to outsiders.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa 32 in Taipei
ld.description: Geographically, it’s only an hour from the airport; figuratively, though, Villa 32 is just about as far as you can get from the clamorous urban cityscape of downtown Taipei. While the vast majority of the city’s high-end business and leisure travelers take in the sights from the top of a city-center high-rise hotel, a fortunate few (just five rooms’ worth) soak in the luxurious solitude of this stunning modernist retreat.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The One Nanyuan in Xinpu
ld.description: The One Nanyuan is a cultural landmark disguised as a retreat, set in the wooded hills of Xinpu and brought to life by Taiwanese architect Han Baode. Inspired by a Song Dynasty painting, the design draws from Jiangnan gardens, Fujian traditions, and Baroque arcades, realized through the work of hundreds of artisans. The result is richly layered, from hand-carved woodwork to winding courtyards. It is a place shaped by philosophy as much as design, where architecture, landscape, and hospitality move in cohesion.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay
